comparison: Both evaluate proteome similarity between hiPSCs and hESCs (C2, C20, C110) and find the evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes >99% overlap and 8491 proteins detected; peer reviewers affirm 'protein expression profiles were found to be very similar' and note 'proteomic evidence is convincing.' OpenEval includes C19 while peer includes C23; both reach the same positive conclusion.

Perfect alignment on claims C3, C24, C29, C30 regarding quantitative proteome differences. Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval highlights 4426/7878 proteins increased and PCA separation; peer reviewers state 'ihPSCs express higher levels of proteins' and editor notes this 'important finding cautions against interchangeable use' of cell types.

Perfect alignment on claims C4, C31-C34 regarding higher protein content in hiPSCs. Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes convergent evidence from MS, EZQ assay, and FACS; peer reviewers explicitly affirm 'verified by an independent approach' and 'flow cytometry confirmed ihPSCs had larger cell size.'

Perfect alignment on claims C5, C35, C36 regarding cell cycle analysis. Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes FACS data rules out cell cycle as confounding variable; peer reviewers accept this finding without challenge, acknowledging flow cytometry data showing no cell cycle differences.

Perfect alignment on claims C25-C28, C96-C97 regarding normalization methods. Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes that median normalization obscures thousands of protein changes; peer reviewers implicitly accept the proteomic ruler approach, with editor noting 'proteomic evidence is convincing' without challenging the methodology.

Strong overlap on nutrient transporter claims (C37-C43 in OpenEval; C37-C43, C44, C46, C47 in peer). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval focuses on proteomic evidence for transporter abundance; peer reviewers emphasize functional validation including 'increased ability to uptake glutamine' as a strength.

Partial overlap on glutamine uptake (C44, C46). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes convergent proteomic and functional validation; peer reviewers include this within broader metabolic findings, noting 'increased ability to uptake glutamine' as validated functional distinction.

Strong overlap on lipid metabolism and droplet formation (C47-C51). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval highlights proteomic data and TEM validation; peer reviewers explicitly mention 'increased ability to form lipid droplets' as validated functional distinction, with TEM evidence unchallenged.

Strong overlap on mitochondrial protein increases (C52-C60 in OpenEval; C52-C63 in peer). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes systematic increases across all mitochondrial categories; peer reviewers affirm 'higher expression of mitochondrial metabolic enzymes' and acknowledge mitochondrial proteins reflect cellular state.

Strong overlap on mitochondrial function validation (C7, C61-C64 in OpenEval; C7, C64 in peer). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes respirometry correlation with proteomic data; peer reviewers explicitly affirm as strength: 'Mitochondrial function was verified by high-resolution respirometry, indicating increased ATP-producing capacity.'

Strong overlap on secreted proteins (C8, C65-C66, C68-C69 in both). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval focuses on systematic increases in secreted protein abundance; peer reviewers accept findings without challenge, though note functional implications require mechanistic explanation.

Overlap on immunosuppressive proteins (C73, C76-C77, C79, C81-C82). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED for proteomic data. OpenEval notes C106 (immune evasion) requires functional validation; peer reviewers accept proteomic findings but don't explicitly evaluate immune evasion speculation.

Minimal overlap on C106 (immune evasion potential). OpenEval evaluates as SUPPORTED with caveat that functional validation needed; peer reviewers evaluate as UNCERTAIN, noting study 'falls short of explaining mechanistic reasons' and functional implications remain uncertain.

Perfect alignment on decreased nuclear proteins (C83-C86, C88-C89). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes small number of decreased proteins enriched in chromatin processes; peer reviewers affirm 'expression of nuclear proteins is similar,' consistent with few nuclear proteins being decreased.

Perfect alignment on histone variant regulation (C90, C92-C93). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval highlights opposing patterns for H1 vs H2 variants with peptide-level validation; peer reviewers accept findings without challenge, not questioning histone variant data.

Strong overlap on summary conclusions (C94-C95, C108-C109 in both; C9 in peer only). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes convergence of proteomic and functional data; peer reviewers affirm 'important finding cautions against interchangeable use' and accept functional validation supports proteomic differences.

Overlap on therapeutic implications (C107). OpenEval evaluates as UNCERTAIN, noting clinical implications require validation beyond study scope; peer reviewers also evaluate as UNCERTAIN, stating study 'falls short of explaining mechanistic reasons' for observed differences.

Perfect alignment on mechanistic uncertainty (C101). OpenEval evaluates as SUPPORTED as appropriate limitation acknowledgment; peer reviewers evaluate as UNCERTAIN, explicitly stating 'it remains unclear whether increased expression is due to enhanced transcription...or other reasons,' confirming mechanistic gap.

Minimal overlap on copy number data (C22-C23 in OpenEval; C23 in peer). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes similar proteome composition and dynamic range as context; peer reviewers include C23 with qualitative similarity findings without specific comment on copy numbers.
